candidate.answerReason: In the usual constant-speed model, Clea's walking covers 2/5 of the escalator length during the 24-second trip. The escalator therefore carries her 3/5 of its length in 24 seconds, so a standing ride takes 40 seconds.

methods.label: Separate the two contributions to distance
methods.explanation:
Use the usual constant-speed model: Clea keeps the same walking pace relative to the steps on both trips, and the operating escalator moves at a constant speed.

Her walking alone covers the escalator's full length in \(60\) seconds. During the \(24\)-second trip, her walking therefore accounts for
\[
\frac{24}{60}=\frac25
\]
of that length. Since walking and the escalator both carry her downward, the escalator supplies the remaining
\[
1-\frac25=\frac35
\]
of the length in those \(24\) seconds.

When Clea stands still, the escalator supplies all the motion. At its constant speed, the time for one full length is
\[
24\div\frac35=24\cdot\frac53=40
\]
seconds, choice \(\mathrm{B}\).
methods.levelReason: Proportional distances and fraction division solve the problem without an algebraic equation.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is using the distance-speed-time relationship and adding simultaneous distance contributions. Direct proportionality supports the 24-second distance calculation, and the method uses fraction division to recover the time for a whole journey. Meeting and catching-up procedures are not used.
